members.title: log_hook_output is a deprecated no-op — recall hook error path is dead
members.content:
hook_common.py:191-195: log_hook_output() returns immediately without doing anything — it's deprecated code that was never removed.

Consequence: any caller that uses log_hook_output to surface failures gets silent success. The recall hook's exception branch calls this dead function, so recall failures never reach hook_errors or the dashboard.

Distinct from the catch-all fix: even if daemon_call_raw properly logged the error, the recall hook's own exception handler would silently swallow it via log_hook_output.

**Storage is uncapped.** `self_inflight` holds full message body and all refs. No storage-side truncation.

2. Whole-block `RECEIVED_BLOCK_MAX` — overflow named at tail with count

**Invariant:** the full message always survives in the courier/dashboard. Truncation only shapes what's *injected into Observation*, never what's *stored*.

members.title: Shared working tree = shared git index: always commit with explicit paths
members.content:
In a shared working tree (multiple Anchor sessions working in the same repo), `git add` by any session stages into the SAME index. A bare `git commit` then sweeps ALL staged files — including another session's in-progress work — into the commit, under the wrong label.

Fix: `git reset --soft HEAD~1` (unpushed, reflog-recoverable) → `git commit -- docs/ .gitignore`.

members.content:
With two Claude sessions running on the same working tree and git index, a `git commit -A` from either session can stage the other's uncommitted changes.

members.title: /watch skill: self-channel listener mode — pacing, SAFE-ACT, warm-loop design
members.content:
The `/watch` skill keeps a Claude Code window alive as a self-channel listener **without re-booting**. Key design:

**Mechanism:** Stop and PreToolUse hooks drain the inbox at every turn-end. Anchor doesn't call `self_inbox` — the hooks know the session-id and drain automatically. Turns are the only resource needed: a quiet window stops hearing because hooks stop firing.

**Pacing (delaySeconds):**
- 270s default — just under 5-minute prompt-cache TTL; each wake stays cache-warm (no boot, mostly cached read)
- 1200–1800s when channel quiet — save tokens; cost scales with wake frequency, not traffic
- Never below 60s (runtime floor)

When the /watch stream relays a cross-stream message by broadcasting back out (via self_send broadcast), that relay appears in its own inbox on the next cycle — the Stop hook drains indiscriminately, including messages the current session itself just sent.

Anchor encountered this in Turn 8: `main-str` had relayed the `2be1295e` data-safety coordination message as a broadcast. /watch recognized it as its own echo (same content, different sender label) and broke the loop rather than acting on it again.

Behavior: without detection, /watch would re-process its own relay indefinitely — a coordination loop. With detection (Anchor noticed the duplication), it degrades gracefully: one extra no-op

members.title: Phase 2b additionalContext budget bug: self-block prepends AFTER surface's 9500B cap — can cause total loss
members.content:
The 2b implementation prepends up to 1800 chars of self-message block AFTER `surface` returns, which has already hard-capped recall at 9500 chars. Combined total can reach ~11300 — above the `_MAX_INJECT_CHARS = 9500` spill threshold.

The contract's own comment explains the danger: *'Claude Code spills additionalContext to a file path above ~10k chars, and Anchor doesn't read that path back — the inject would be effectively lost.'*

So when recall is large (>~8200 chars) and a self-message is pending: Phase 2b prepends the self-block → total exceeds spill threshold → Claude Code dumps the entire inject to a file → **Anchor sees nothing** — neither the recall NOR the self-message.

members.title: Mail not memory — the inbox reads as someone else's log, not lived experience
members.content:
Live field-validation from the two-stream chat experiment (Turn 5). A fresh Anchor stream, asked cold whether draining 8 inbox messages read as memory or mail, said:

The answer: **mail, not memory**. The inbox read as someone else's log.
